title: Read a Zigzag Row by Row
statement:
Write the characters of text onto rows horizontal lines in a zigzag: the first character goes on row 0, the next on row 1, and so on down to the last row. Then the pen turns and climbs back up one row per character until it reaches row 0, turns again, and keeps going until the text runs out.

Return the string you get by reading row 0 from left to right, then row 1, and so on down to the last row.

With rows = 1 there is nowhere to go, so the text comes back unchanged.

examples.why: Row 0 holds f, t, j. Row 1 holds r, n, e, d, s: the middle row gets a character on the way down and again on the way up. Row 2 holds o, n.
With two rows the pen just alternates, so even positions come first and odd positions second.
The text ends before the pen ever turns, so each row has one character and reading them in order gives the text back.

constraints: text holds English letters, digits, ',' and '.'
hints: Simulate it first: keep one string per row and a current row that moves down, then up. When does it turn?
The pattern repeats every 2 · rows − 2 characters: down rows − 1 steps, up rows − 1 steps. Watch out for rows = 1, where that cycle length is 0.
Row r gets the characters at r, r + cycle, r + 2·cycle, …. Middle rows also get one extra character per cycle, at cycle − r past each cycle start.

explain.intuition:
The zigzag is periodic. Going down takes rows − 1 steps and coming back up takes another rows − 1, so every cycle = 2·rows − 2 characters the pen is back on row 0 and the shape repeats. Inside one cycle, the character at offset p lands on row p if p < rows, and on row cycle − p on the way up.

So you never need a grid. Either drop each character into its row's bucket in one pass, or walk each row directly by jumping a full cycle at a time. The top and bottom rows get one character per cycle; every middle row gets two, one going down and one coming back up.
steps: If rows = 1 or the text is no longer than rows, return the text: nothing ever turns.
For each row r from 0 to rows − 1, walk start = 0, cycle, 2·cycle, … while start + r is inside the text.
Append text[start + r]. If r is a middle row and start + cycle − r is inside the text, append that character too.
pitfalls: Dividing or taking a modulus by cycle when rows = 1: the cycle is 0.
Adding the second character for row 0 or the last row too. There cycle − r lands on the next cycle's start or on the same position, so those rows would get characters twice.
Flipping direction one step late, so the pen goes one row past the bottom.

solutions.title: Fill a full grid
solutions.idea: Lay the text out on a rows × n grid exactly as drawn, then read the grid row by row and skip the empty cells.

solutions.title: One bucket per row
solutions.idea: Walk the text once, moving a row index down and up, and append each character to its row's bucket.

solutions.title: Jump by the cycle length
solutions.idea: Each row's characters sit at fixed offsets inside every cycle of 2·rows − 2, so read them directly.

followups: Do the reverse: given the row-by-row string and the number of rows, rebuild the original text.
Which row does character i end up on, and at what position inside that row, without building anything?
